sec1.2.title: Edit setting value
cover.title: Platform Management
p3s1i0: A screen that shows, in one table, the operation policies applied across the whole platform. It is not a place to change values directly. It is where you check which policy is set to which value. Only items that can be changed open an edit window.
p3.cap.1: System settings (SCR-PLT-004) — security, session, notification, file and general operation policies
p3s2i0: Category tabs — All · Security · Session · Notification · File · General. Workspace administrators see only Session · Notification.
p3s2i1: Editable status — Use this to hide locked items and show only the items you can change.
p3s2i2: Search — Find items by setting key or by part of the description.
p3s2i3: Reset — Clears all the conditions you have set.
p3s2i4: Edit — Opens the window that changes that item's value 1.2. Locked items show a faded button and cannot be selected.
p3s2i5: The only entry point to this screen is Platform menu > System settings in the left menu.
p3s2i6: The note “※ Changes are recorded in the operation history.” at the top — to see who changed what and when, check the operation history 4.1.
p3s2i7: Type — The format of the value, such as integer, true/false or JSON. The input method in the edit window depends on this type.
p3s2i8: Status — Editable or 🔒Locked. Locked items are fixed by the system, so even administrators cannot change them.
p3s2i9: Last modified (KST) — Shows - if the value has never been changed.
p3s2i10: The English text under an item name is its setting key. Use this key when you search or look up the operation history.
p3s3i0: Values changed here are not applied to current system behavior. Values and change history are saved, but actual decisions such as the login lock threshold and session expiry are made by separate settings. The impact note in each edit window tells you this for that item, so be sure to check it 1.2.
p4.title: Edit setting value
p4s1i0: The window that opens when you select Edit in the table. It is a simple window for changing one value, but the Impact scope note at the top tells you whether that value is actually used. Read it before you change anything.
p4.cap.1: Edit window — the setting key, category and type are shown together at the top (enlarged)
p4s2i0: Value — Enter it in the format that matches the type. For an integer item, a notice appears before saving if the value is outside the recommended range.
p4s2i1: Reason for change — Optional. If you enter a reason, it is recorded in the operation history together with the change, so it is good practice to note why you made the change.
p4s2i2: Restore default — Only fills the input field with the default value. Selecting this alone does not save the change, so you must then select Save.
p4s2i3: Save — Applies the value. Select Cancel next to it to discard the change and close the window.
p4s2i4: The setting key · category · type are shown together at the top of the window. Check here that you have not opened a different item.
p4s2i5: The yellow Impact scope note tells you whether that value is actually applied in system behavior. Check the precautions below.
p4s2i6: Change history — The change log for this item only. If the count is 0, the value has never been changed.
p4s2i8: Selecting outside the window or selecting close has the same effect.
p4s3i0: Every item is currently shown as “not applied”. Values and change history are saved, but actual decisions such as login lock and session expiry are made in separate settings. If a policy must actually change, this screen alone is not enough. Ask the system administrator.
p5.title: Screen layout
ch2.title: Code management
sec2.1.title: Screen layout
sec2.2.title: Add code value
p5s1i0: A screen that manages the standard codes used by dropdowns and badges across the screens. Pick a code group on the left, and the list of values for that group appears on the right in a two-pane layout. Subject status, site type and reasons for a missed visit all come from here.
p5.cap.1: Code management (SCR-PLT-005) — code groups on the left, values of the selected group on the right
p5s2i0: Platform / Project tabs — Platform codes are shared by all projects. Project codes apply only to that project. The Project tab opens only after you enter a project.
p5s2i1: + Add value — Adds a code value to the selected group 2.2.
p5s2i2: Row actions — the pencil on the left is Edit (label and sort order). The button on the right switches the value between active and inactive. When you switch from active to inactive, a confirmation window appears once more.
p5s2i3: When you select a code group, the list of values on the right switches to that group.
p5s2i4: The only entry point to this screen is Platform menu > Code management in the left menu.
p5s2i5: The note “※ Changes are recorded in the operation history.” — code changes are also recorded in the operation history 4.1.
p5s2i6: The group header shows the group code · scope · number of values · type. A group whose type is SYSTEM holds the standard codes preloaded by the system.
p5s2i7: Columns — CODE · LABEL · SORTORDER · Status · Last modified (KST) · Actions. The text shown on screen is LABEL, not CODE.
p5s2i8: Status — A value switched to inactive can no longer be selected for new entries, but data already saved with that value stays as it is.
p5s2i9: Search is available separately on the left (groups) and on the right (values).
p5s3i0: Only system administrators can edit platform-wide codes. Workspace administrators and data managers can edit only the codes on the Project tab, and that tab opens only when you are inside a project.
p6.title: Add code value
p6s1i0: Adds one code value to the selected group. Code is the value the system stores, and Label is the text shown on screen. If you confuse the two, the screen may look correct while the stored value is different, so take care.
p6.cap.1: New code value — only Code and Label are required (enlarged)
p6s2i0: Code * — The value stored in the system. Use 1 to 50 letters, numbers or underscores. It cannot be changed after creation.
p6s2i1: Label * — The text shown on screen. You can edit it later.
p6s2i2: Value type — Text is the default. You can usually leave it as it is.
p6s2i3: Sort order — The position in the list. If left blank, it is assigned automatically.
p6s2i4: Add — Creates the value. Selecting Cancel next to it discards your input.
p6s2i5: The target group is shown at the top of the window. Check here that you are not adding the value to a different group.
p6s2i6: Below the Code field, the usable characters and length are shown, together with the note that it cannot be changed.
p6s2i7: Value type note — text is recommended.
p6s2i8: Sort order note — if left blank, the last value + 1 is assigned automatically.
p6s2i9: Cancel — Closes the window and creates nothing.
p6s3i0: A code cannot be changed after it is created. If data is already saved with that code, there is no way to roll the value back, so check the code scheme used in your research standards or report forms before you enter a code. Mark a value created by mistake as inactive instead of deleting it.
p7.title: Screen layout
ch3.title: Access log
sec3.1.title: Screen layout
sec3.2.title: Search, filter and summary
sec3.3.title: CSV export
p7s1i0: A screen that records who accessed the system, when and from where. Records are append-only, with no editing or deletion, so they are the first source for checking account misuse or abnormal access. System administrators see everything. Workspace administrators see the scope of their own workspace.
p7.cap.1: Access log (SCR-PLT-006) — login, logout and session events
p7s2i0: CSV export — Saves the current results as a file 3.3.
p7s2i1: User · IP address · Start date · End date — Narrows the search range 3.2.
p7s2i2: Event — Select one of nine types, such as login success or failure, logout, or e-signature failure 3.2.
p7s2i3: Reset — Clears all the conditions you have set.
p7s2i4: The Platform menu > Access log in the left menu is always available. You can also open it from a user's details in User management, already filtered to that user.
p7s2i5: Next to the buttons, current results N / total N appears. Check the precautions below.
p7s2i6: Three summary cards — top failed IPs · account lock · logins in the last 24h 3.2.
p7s2i7: Columns — Time (KST) · User · Event · IP / UA · Reason. The small text under the IP is the program used for the connection (UA).
p7s2i8: Event badges — failure-type events are shown in red, so they stand out at a glance.
p7s2i9: The subtitle “(Cannot be edited or deleted)” means that records cannot be deleted or changed.
p7s3i0: The table moves only by Previous / Next, not by page number. Because records keep accumulating, page boundaries can shift and rows may repeat or go missing. For that reason the system does not provide page-number navigation.
p8.title: Search, filter and summary
p8s1i0: There are five search conditions, and they apply together. The three summary cards below summarize the results, but they count only the 20 records loaded on the current page, and you must keep that in mind.
p8.cap.1: Search conditions — four fields and one event (enlarged)
p8.cap.2: Summary cards (3) — all based on the current page (enlarged)
p8s2i0: User — Narrows the results to one account.
p8s2i1: IP address — Must match the full address. If you enter only part of it, the results are not filtered.
p8s2i2: Start date — The first date of the search.
p8s2i3: End date — The last date of the search. Use it together with the start date to set a period.
p8s2i5: Event — Only one can be selected at a time. Selecting the chip again clears it.
p8s2i6: The note in the User field — if you came from a user's details in User management, that account is entered automatically.
p8s2i7: The note in the IP field — an example format is shown.
p8s2i8: Top failed IPs (top 5) — The IPs where login failures are concentrated. If failures keep repeating from the same IP, you can suspect an attempt at account misuse.
p8s2i9: Account lock — The number of lock events.
p8s2i10: Logins in the last 24h — The number of successful and failed logins.
p8s2i11: All three cards show the current page at the bottom. Check the precautions below.
p8s3i0: The three summary cards count only the 20 records on the current page, not the whole data set. “No top failed IPs” or “Account lock 0” means there are none on this page, not that there are none for the whole period. To see the full picture, set the event filter to Login failure or Account lock and search again.
p9.title: CSV export
p9s1i0: Downloads the search results as a comma-separated file (CSV). The file is created right on screen, with no separate request or waiting, and the time of the download is included in the file name.
p9.cap.1: Click the button to download the file immediately (enlarged)
p9s2i0: CSV export — Click it and the file downloads immediately, without a confirmation window.
p9s2i1: Next to the button, the count appears as current results N / total N (full export not supported). Check the precautions below.
p9s2i2: The download notification shows the file name and size. The file name follows the format login-history_yyyymmddThhmm.csv.
p9s2i3: Seven columns — Time (KST) · Name · Email · Event · IP address · Access program (UA) · Failure reason. Internal identification codes are not included.
p9s2i4: One row is one access event. The rows follow the same order as the table on screen.
p9s3i0: Only the current page of results is downloaded. The note “full export not supported” next to the button means exactly that. To download the whole period, narrow the period and event conditions and download in several batches. The file contains account emails and access IP addresses as they are, so handle it as a file containing personal data when you store or share it.
p10.title: Screen layout
ch4.title: Operation history
sec4.1.title: Screen layout
sec4.2.title: View details
p10s1i0: A screen that records who changed what for accounts, projects, participating organizations, workspaces and system settings. If the access log is a record of who came and went, this one is a record of what was changed. It is also append-only, with no editing or deletion.
p10.cap.1: Operation history (SCR-PLT-007) — records of operations on accounts, projects, organizations and the system
p10s2i0: Category tabs — Group the records by account management · project status transitions · test data deletion · Site management · staff management · workspace members · system setting changes · EXPORT.
p10s2i1: Event — Narrows the records by type of action, such as create, edit or delete.
p10s2i2: Target type — Narrows the records by what was changed, such as account, project or site.
p10s2i3: Performed-by ID — Shows only the actions of a specific user. The full identifier must match.
p10s2i4: CSV/Excel export — Requests a file of the search results.
p10s2i5: View — Opens the detail window for that row 4.2. What changed and how it changed can be checked only in this window.
p10s2i6: The Platform menu > Operation history in the left menu is always available.
p10s2i7: The note “※ Clinical data change history (Audit Trail) is provided on a separate screen.” — Records of changes made to subject data are in Audit Trail, not here.
p10s2i8: Target column — Currently the front part is shown as undefined. See the precautions below.
p10s2i9: Details column — Shows the names of the changed items as a summary. To see the values, select View.
p10s2i10: Start date · End date — Sets the period.
p10s3i0: The undefined shown at the front of the Target column is a display defect. The system does not yet know the name of this type of target, so it shows that. The record itself is not wrong. Judge what was changed by the Category column, the identifier attached after it, and the change details in View.
p11.title: View details
p11s1i0: A window that opens with View in the list. The list shows when, who and what. This window adds how it changed. It is read-only, and nothing can be edited here.
p11.cap.1: Operation history details — changed values are listed by item (enlarged)
p11s2i0: Close — Closes the window and returns to the list. Selecting outside the window has the same effect.
p11s2i1: The header shows time · category · event on one line.
p11s2i2: Target — The same value as the target column in the list. The undefined at the front is a display defect, so use the identifier after it (see the note in 4.1).
p11s2i3: Performed by — The user who carried out the action. If an email was recorded with it, it is added below.
p11s2i4: Change details (DETAILS) — The core of this window. Each changed item is listed as a pair of name and value.
p11s2i5: Item names are in English because the window shows the system's internal names as they are. The screenshot is a record of a CRF form edit, so the version, form code, edit scope and project status are kept together.
p11s3i0: The operation history contains only operation and administration actions. Records of changes to subject data are in the separate Audit Trail screen, so when you prepare regulatory materials, check both screens together.
